Lead story image inside the card link for 'Arrest made in connection with hijacking of car in Cork'. The crop and the file name show a generic stock photo of a Garda in a hi-vis jacket seen from behind. Its alt is the article's figcaption pasted in with literal

tags (the article page has the same text as its figcaption): an appeal for witnesses at Curraheen Road Sports Grounds between 1pm and 2pm, which the picture does not show, and nothing about what it does show. It is exposed in the link name, so screen readers read the markup and the caption before the headline. As a text alternative it neither describes the image nor is null for a decorative stock picture, so it does not serve the equivalent purpose (1.1.1). The claim points at that defect. captureDiffers: the homepage has changed since capture; the same picture now appears as a small teaser with alt 'Garda stock', so the live page no longer shows this alt. Judged from the capture, which is what users received when Rampa read it.

The claim that it describes something the image does not show is false, and the alt is an adequate alternative for an illustrative photo inside a link whose headline gives its purpose, so 1.1.1 is met. captureDiffers: the story has since rotated off the live homepage; judged from the capture. The model had the crop and misjudged it.

The alt repeats the headline quote; the crop shows the actress (with others) posing outdoors in Cork, so LA and rain are not shown and the sentence is literally true. But the image sits in a link whose text gives the purpose, and the alt identifies the story's subject, the actor pictured; a redundant alt equal to the headline is a best-practice matter (H2), not a 1.1.1 failure, and no documented failure covers it. Live page unchanged for this image.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: Header social link, icon only, aria-label 'instagram', to https://www.instagram.com/echolive.ie/. The visible links with that name are this one, the sidebar 'Instagram' (same address plus ?hl=en) and the footer 'instagram' (same address); a fourth copy in the sub-navigation is hidden. ?hl=en only sets Instagram's interface language, so all resolve to the same profile (R1: same resource), and the sidebar and footer links are also told apart by their preceding headings (FOLLOW ECHO, Follow Us). So the claim's 'two different places' is false and the purpose, the site's Instagram account, is clear from the name: 2.4.4 is met. Rampa did not read the destinations. Live page has the same links.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The 'Search' button of the myhome.ie property widget in the sidebar. The widget's live stylesheet (media.myhome.ie/cdn/widget/styles.css) sets #mh-search {background:#009cdb; color:#fff; font-weight:bold}, and the screenshot shows white bold text on that blue. White on #009cdb is 3.10:1; at 13px bold this is not large text (needs 14pt bold), so 1.4.3 requires 4.5:1. The claim states the colours and ratio correctly. Third-party widget, but it is part of the page.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: 'MORE' in the main navigation, href='#', a hover/click toggle for a dropdown. Its list item (part of its programmatically determined context under this rubric) contains the dropdown's links: Advertise with us, Mini Marathon 2026, Find a House, Find a Job, Competitions, Photosales, Subscribe, epaper, Contact Us and so on, so what the control reveals can be determined from its context and the claim that nothing around it tells is false. Exposing a menu toggle as a link without aria-expanded is a 4.1.2 matter, not 2.4.4. The live page has the same markup. Rampa had the list item text in its ancestors.
